title: Procurement decisions and closing accounts
question: What changed between the original decision, the signed authority and the payment register?
finding: 16 cases connect source records across stages of a public decision.
how: Match the project, contract, payee or account identifier. Reconstruct the decision under the rules and appropriations in force in that period.
limits: The source in each row identifies the decision. Each case distinguishes the authority to spend from the actual payment and names the outstanding evidence.

rows.test: What was paid on the airport design subcontract, which clients appeared in the amended disclosures and did any have business before the commissioner?
rows.record: Frank Fung managed and half-owned ED2 International while it earned $39,460 for airport design work. His amended disclosures identify the three clients behind seven omissions.
rows.limit: Obtain the executed ARUP and ED2 subcontract, itemized design deliverables and acceptance records, ED2 invoices and any case-specific penalty remittance.

source.t: 651 Geary conditional-use staff report and drawings, ED2 and Success Development

rows.test: What did the grant authorize, how much was actually paid, and where did investigators trace the proceeds?
rows.record: Barbara Mumby overruled an eligibility check and secured a larger grant advance. Investigators traced the money to a group trip and a $3,500 deposit in her account.
rows.limit: Obtain the grant agreement and public project description, payment authorizations, accepted deliverables, final report, any grant-recovery ledger entry and the administrative penalty receipt.

source.t: Original FY18–19 IAC recommendation packet, pp. 1–2, 12 and 30–40, funding recommendation and contemporaneous grant guidelines

rows.test: Which City payments, third-party invoices and credits comprise the Wong settlement, and what portion was due in cash?
rows.record: Four emergency contracts, a planter invoice and utility purchases figured in the settlement. Some of its value came from canceled bills and credit for goods the City kept.
rows.limit: Obtain the executed agreement, City receivable closeout, receipts for the two installments and disposition of the bank letter. Match the federal restitution disbursement to the City’s receipt.

source.t: Settlement exhibit, recitals and sections 1–10, plus approved resolution

rows.test: Did either land-use decision follow the contact, who voted, and which compensation did the order actually cover?
rows.record: Claudine Cheng received about $1,500 for services tied to three prohibited contacts. Her separate lobbyist reports and the Planning Commission’s roll call document the permit outcome.
rows.limit: Reconcile the administrative fine with the Ethics Commission penalty receipt and Controller cash ledger for complaint 12-130819.

rows.test: Can the amended filings and a documented recusal establish which income sources had a matter pending during the disclosure period?
rows.record: David Wasserman reported income but left 28 qualifying sources unnamed over four years. The Ethics Commission imposed a $16,800 fine after he amended the disclosures.
rows.limit: Request the four original, pre-amendment filings and a redacted record of penalty collection to complete the original-to-corrected filing comparison and City cash reconciliation.

source.t: Fully executed order 23-598, Exhibit A, pages 5–8

rows.test: Does pre-conversion spending explain the apparent gap in the modern CleanPowerSF contract register, and what remained wrong in the Board filing?
rows.record: The utility sent the Board a contract ceiling $170,084.60 below the amount its Commission approved. Two earlier payments explain why the same difference appears in the modern register.
rows.limit: Obtain the signed fourth and fifth amendments, the May 2024 calculation sheet used to prepare the Board submission, and invoice-to-contract coding for the eight direct fiscal 2017–18 Calpine payments.

rows.test: Which targets were missing in the monitoring system, how much was paid under site-specific contracts and how did the City follow up?
rows.record: The City left the Stanford Hotel’s property management targets out of its reporting system. Its review documented 18 findings across two programs.
rows.limit: Obtain the site visit reports, the two programs’ final monitoring and closure letters, and aggregate monthly measures after HSH configured CARBON. Request the subsequent fiscal status for the three organization-wide findings.

source.t: December 3, 2025 analyst report, File 251147, page 18 and footnotes 4–5

rows.test: Which political contributions reached either side of the 2002 public power vote before the deadline, when were they disclosed and which regulator handled each settlement?
rows.record: Two October checks totaling $800,000 to the committee opposing Proposition D were disclosed after the election. A separate order documents four late reports by the committee supporting it.
rows.limit: Obtain the two City installment receipts, the separate state court judgment and satisfaction, and the Yes committee’s $267 receipt.

source.t: Decision and stipulation 49-021130, including the two checks, filing dates and mitigation

rows.test: Which county was entitled to the electricity tax, which account was exempt, and who actually received the corrective payments?
rows.record: SFPUC applied San Francisco’s tax to two electric accounts in unincorporated Alameda County. Supervisors authorized $754,141 in corrections. Three Controller vouchers show $754,139.82 paid to the affected parties.
rows.limit: Match the interfund transfer and tax-collection ledger to the three refund vouchers and check subsequent out-of-county accounts for the correct tax rate and exemption.

source.t: Enacted resolution 474-24, named recipients and authorized amounts

rows.test: Does the signed grant ceiling include every scheduled year, and which early payments appear under different contract numbers?
rows.record: The original agreement listed a $572,765 subsidy in 2039 yet left that year out of the grant total. Supervisors corrected the ceiling. The first three scheduled amounts match three separate City payment entries.
rows.limit: Obtain the executed first amendment and approved program payment schedule, including the unrounded annual estimates, actual initial leasing date, and reconciliation across the separate contract identifiers.

source.t: Original April 2024 senior operating subsidy grant and annual schedule

rows.test: How much of the change arose from inspection hours and rates, and how much actually posted against the agreement?
rows.record: The budget for inspecting Mountain Tunnel assumed fewer hours and a lower average rate than SFPUC later needed. A $9.5 million amendment raised the management contract ceiling to $34 million. The approved construction-management budget was $40.8 million.
rows.limit: Obtain inspection shift plans, accepted hours, individual task authorizations, final invoices and the project closeout to compare estimates with actual activity.

source.t: Original Mountain Tunnel construction management services agreement

rows.test: In which pay periods did spending first exceed authority, when did supervisors act, and do the final spending and appropriation totals reconcile?
rows.record: The Sheriff exceeded its overtime budget before the Board approved more money in three consecutive fiscal years. In 2026 the Board moved $1.55 million out of jail projects to help pay for overtime.
rows.limit: Obtain the certified closing control ledger for funds 10000 and 10060, dated accounting transfers and the status of funding restored to jail projects.

source.t: Administrative Code section 3.17, Separate Overtime Appropriations

rows.test: How did the engineering selection change after the protest, and what do the final award and payment records establish?
rows.record: The City posted Stantec/AGS as the highest-scoring team. A sustained protest exposed a qualification that the first review missed.
rows.limit: Obtain the complete November 20 final determination, protest, proposer reply, screening worksheet and original qualification requirements from the commission secretary. Obtain training attendance and subsequent quality reviews.

source.t: PRO.0164 original solicitation and notices to proposers, especially May 22, 2020

rows.test: Which plumbing bids survived review, and what happened to the disputed award?
rows.record: Airco challenged the two lower plumbing bids. Its lawyer invoked a Local 38 rule at the hearing, and four directors awarded the work to Desert Mechanical.
rows.limit: Obtain Airco’s original and updated protest letters, September 4 bidder replies, final determination letters, executed trade agreements, fabrication submittals and any written Local 38 accommodations.

source.t: Approved November 10 minutes, item 7 and Resolution 11-041

rows.test: How did the law in force on the date of the solicitation affect the highest-scoring baggage maintenance proposal?
rows.record: SFO disqualified its incumbent because its United States headquarters was in Georgia. The replacement firm later won a new competition after the City repealed the ban.
rows.limit: Obtain bidder score sheets, the competing 2022 price proposals, actual reimbursed costs and corrective records for tracking accuracy.

source.t: March 2022 covered-state list, including operative dates and Georgia grounds

rows.test: Did a commissioner vote on a project involving his firm, and how did the agency resolve the design competitions?
rows.record: Two disqualifications left one eligible architect. Its bid listed a sitting design reviewer’s firm for $2.7 million in labor. SFPUC rescinded the award and ran a third competition.
rows.limit: Obtain final payment ledgers and task orders for the third agreement, delivered social impact commitments and reconciled project escalation, finance and schedule records.

source.t: September 2021 solicitation PRO.0232, qualification and overhead and profit schedules
